About My Village

History, nature and people of Dharmapuri

Dharmapuri lies in the north-western corner of Tamil Nadu, close to the Karnataka border, surrounded by the hills of the Eastern Ghats. In the Sangam age it was called Thagadur and was the capital of the chieftain Adhiyaman Neduman Anji. He is remembered in Tamil literature (Purananuru) for giving a rare nellikani (gooseberry) that could grant long life to the poetess Avvaiyar, believing that her poetry was more valuable to the world than his own life.

Over the centuries the region was ruled by the Pallavas, Cholas, Hoysalas, the Vijayanagara empire, the Mysore kingdom under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, and finally the British after 1792. Dharmapuri district was formed on 2 October 1965 by separating it from Salem district, and in 2004 the Krishnagiri district was carved out of it.

The river Kaveri enters Tamil Nadu here at the famous Hogenakkal Falls, and the Hogenakkal drinking water project supplies water to lakhs of people in Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri. Most people depend on agriculture – mango, tamarind, ragi, millets, groundnut, sugarcane and paddy are grown here. Dharmapuri is also known for silk weaving, granite quarrying and its large tamarind trade.

The people are known for their simple lifestyle, warm hospitality and colourful temple festivals that bring the whole village together. Tamil is the main language, and Kannada and Telugu are also spoken because of the nearness to Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

Places to Visit

Famous spots in and around Dharmapuri – click “Book” to reserve

Hogenakkal Falls

Waterfall · Coracle Ride

Called the “Niagara of India”. The name comes from Kannada words meaning “smoking rocks”, because the spray rising from the falls looks like smoke. Here the Kaveri river enters Tamil Nadu and splits into many streams that fall over some of the oldest carbonatite rocks in Asia. Visitors ride the round bamboo coracle (parisal) boats right up to the falls, take a traditional oil massage on the rocks, cross the hanging bridge, climb the view tower and enjoy fresh river fish fry cooked on the riverbank.

  • 📍 Location: Hogenakkal, Pennagaram Taluk, Dharmapuri – 636810
  • 🚗 About 46 km west of Dharmapuri town
  • 🕒 6 AM – 6 PM · Best: Aug to Jan

Adhiyaman Kottam (Avvaiyar Memorial)

History · Heritage

A memorial built by the Tamil Nadu government to honour King Adhiyaman Neduman Anji and the great poetess Avvaiyar. The golden statues show the famous moment when the king gives Avvaiyar the rare nellikani of long life. The walls are covered with colourful paintings showing the life of Adhiyaman, his battles and the Sangam-age history of Thagadur. It is a popular place for students and history lovers.

  • 📍 Location: Adhiyamankottai, Salem Main Road (NH 44), Dharmapuri – 636807
  • 🚗 About 7 km from Dharmapuri town
  • 🕒 9 AM – 6 PM · Open all days
🗺️ Map

Chennaraya Perumal Temple

Temple · ASI Monument

An ancient stone temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Chennaraya Perumal), built during the Vijayanagara period and protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. It is famous for its rare ceiling paintings (murals) that tell stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and for its beautiful carved stone walls and tower. The peaceful lawn around the temple makes it a lovely place to sit and relax.

  • 📍 Location: Adhiyamankottai, Dharmapuri – 636807
  • 🚗 About 7 km from Dharmapuri town
  • 🕒 7 AM – 12 PM, 4 PM – 7 PM
🗺️ Map
Photo: Chennaraya Perumal Temple, Adhiyamankottai

Theerthamalai Temple

Temple · Hill

A hill temple of Lord Shiva as Theerthagireeswarar, built against a huge rocky cliff. The hill has several natural springs (theerthams) such as Rama Theertham and Kumara Theertham – legend says Lord Rama worshipped Shiva here and created a spring with his arrow. Devotees believe a bath in these springs is holy. The climb takes about an hour, and the Masi Magam festival draws large crowds.

  • 📍 Location: Theerthamalai, Harur Taluk, Dharmapuri – 636906
  • 🚗 About 60 km east of Dharmapuri (16 km from Harur)
  • 🕒 6 AM – 6 PM · Start the climb early
🗺️ Map
Photo: Theerthamalai temple below the rocky hill

Vathalmalai Hills

Hills · Trekking

A small, unspoiled hill station of the Eastern Ghats at about 1,300 metres, reached by a winding ghat road with many hairpin bends. It has cool weather all year, misty mornings, thick green forests and small tribal (Malayali) villages that grow millets, jackfruit and pepper. It is a great place for trekking, bird watching, photography and a peaceful day away from the city.

  • 📍 Location: Vathalmalai, Dharmapuri Taluk – 636705
  • 🚗 About 25 km from Dharmapuri town
  • 🕒 Daytime visit · Best: Sep to Feb
🗺️ Map
Photo: misty forests of Vathalmalai

Mango Farm Visit

Farm · Village Life

Dharmapuri and nearby Krishnagiri are among the biggest mango-growing areas of Tamil Nadu, with thousands of acres of orchards. On a farm visit you walk through the mango groves, see how farmers grow, pick and pack the fruit, and taste fresh Neelam, Bangalora (Totapuri), Banganapalli and Alphonso mangoes straight from the tree. Many farms also sell mango pulp, pickles and juice made locally.

  • 📍 Location: Palacode / Karimangalam area, Dharmapuri
  • 🚗 About 20–30 km from Dharmapuri town
  • 🕒 Best: April to June (mango season)

Veerappan – The Forest Brigand

A dark chapter in the history of the Dharmapuri – Sathyamangalam forests

Image: poster from the documentary “The Hunt for Veerappan”

Quick Facts

  • Full nameKoose Munisamy Veerappan
  • Born18 January 1952
  • BirthplaceGopinatham, Kollegal, Karnataka
  • Known forSandalwood smuggling, ivory poaching
  • Active areaForests of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka & Kerala
  • Died18 October 2004 (age 52)
  • Place of deathPapparapatti, Dharmapuri district
  • Buried atMoolakkadu, near Mettur

🌱 Early Life

Veerappan was born on 18 January 1952 in the small forest village of Gopinatham near the Tamil Nadu – Karnataka border. Growing up close to the forests, he started poaching elephants for ivory and cutting sandalwood trees as a teenager with a local gang.

🌲 Life as a Smuggler

For nearly 30 years he hid in about 6,000 sq. km of thick forests spread across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala – including the Sathyamangalam, MM Hills and Hogenakkal–Pennagaram forests near Dharmapuri. His gang smuggled around 65 tonnes of sandalwood and killed hundreds of elephants for ivory. He was easily recognised by his famous thick, curled moustache.

⚠️ Crimes and Kidnappings

Veerappan is believed to have killed about 184 people, around half of them police and forest officers. In 1991 he killed forest officer P. Srinivas. In July 2000 he kidnapped the famous Kannada actor Dr. Rajkumar and held him for 108 days before releasing him. In 2002 he kidnapped former Karnataka minister H. Nagappa, who was later found dead in the forest. The governments of both states spent hundreds of crores of rupees trying to catch him.

🎯 His Death – Operation Cocoon

On 18 October 2004, the Tamil Nadu Special Task Force (STF) led by K. Vijay Kumar carried out “Operation Cocoon”. An undercover officer tricked Veerappan into coming out of the forest for eye treatment and he got into a fake ambulance. At Papparapatti in Dharmapuri district, the ambulance was stopped and surrounded by the STF, and Veerappan and his men were killed in the gunfight. This ended one of the longest manhunts in Indian history.

Today, the forests where he once hid are peaceful again, and areas like Hogenakkal have become safe and popular tourist spots.

Culture & Food

What makes our village special

🎉

Festivals

Pongal is the biggest festival – houses are decorated with kolam, cattle are honoured on Mattu Pongal and families cook sweet pongal together. Deepavali, Aadi Perukku (river festival on the Kaveri), Masi Magam and village temple car (ther) festivals are celebrated with great joy.

🍛

Food

Ragi kali (finger millet balls) with keerai or chicken curry, kambu koozh (pearl millet drink) in summer, crispy fish fry from Hogenakkal, and sweet mangoes and tamarind dishes are local favourites. Meals are traditionally served on banana leaves.

🌾

Agriculture

Farming is the backbone of Dharmapuri. Farmers grow mango, tamarind, ragi, millets, groundnut, sugarcane, paddy and vegetables. Dry-land farming with rainwater is common, and many villages also raise cattle, goats and silkworms for silk.

🥁

Folk Arts

Traditional folk arts like Karagattam (dancing with a decorated pot on the head), Oyilattam, Kummi, Kolattam and the powerful beats of the Parai drum are performed during temple festivals and village celebrations.
